questions.question_text: Calculate the amount if R5000 is invested at 8% p.a. compound interest for 3 years.

common_mistakes.explanation: Compound interest uses A = P(1+i)ⁿ, not A = P(1+in)
8% = 0.08 as a decimal

questions.question_text: R10000 is invested at 12% p.a. compounded monthly. Calculate the value after 2 years.
questions.explanation:
Monthly compounding:
i = 12%/12 = 1% = 0.01 per month
n = 2 × 12 = 24 months

A = P(1 + i)ⁿ
A = 10000(1.01)²⁴
A = 10000(1.26973)
A = R12697.35

common_mistakes.explanation: Divide rate by 12, multiply time by 12
Must use monthly rate: 12%/12 = 1% per month

questions.question_text: How long will it take for an investment to double at 9% p.a. compound interest? Give your answer in years (rounded to 1 decimal place).
hints: Use logarithms to solve for n
questions.explanation:
A = P(1 + i)ⁿ
2P = P(1.09)ⁿ
2 = (1.09)ⁿ

Taking log of both sides:
log 2 = n × log 1.09
n = log 2 / log 1.09
n = 0.301 / 0.0374
n ≈ 8.04 years ≈ 8.0 years

common_mistakes.explanation: To solve for n in the exponent, use logs
n = ln2/ln1.09 works the same way

questions.question_text: A home loan of R800000 at 10.5% p.a. compounded monthly is repaid over 20 years. Calculate the balance owing after 5 years of payments.
hints: Then find balance = PV of remaining payments
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate monthly payment
i = 10.5%/12 = 0.875% = 0.00875
n = 20 × 12 = 240
P = R800000

x = Pi/[1-(1+i)⁻ⁿ]
x = 800000 × 0.00875 / [1-(1.00875)⁻²⁴⁰]
x = 7000 / 0.8756
x = R7994.97

Step 2: Balance after 5 years (180 payments remaining)
Balance = x[1-(1+i)⁻¹⁸⁰]/i
Balance = 7994.97[1-(1.00875)⁻¹⁸⁰]/0.00875
Balance = 7994.97 × 88.524
Balance ≈ R707621

common_mistakes.explanation: After 5 years: 20-5 = 15 years = 180 months remaining
Balance is PV of remaining payments, not original loan minus payments made

questions.question_text: A car depreciates at 15% p.a. on a reducing balance. If it is worth R180000 now, what will it be worth in 4 years?

common_mistakes.explanation: Depreciation decreases value, so subtract the rate
Reducing balance uses exponential decay, not linear
